title: Truthfulness
hook: the kind lie: an empty dipper on one side, a burning house on the other
tomorrow: what would you say if the truth cost you your freedom?

segments.voice: Yesterday Punna named each hard thing plainly and dropped the grumble. No complaints. Plain naming leads straight into today's perfection.

A friend shows you the haircut she can't undo. A grandparent asks if they're still a good driver. The kind lie is right there on your tongue. Buddhists have argued about this one, and both sides lean on texts they hold sacred. One side starts from the precept: refrain from false speech. The other starts from a story about a burning house.
screen: `THE HAIRCUT SHE CAN'T UNDO.` → `THE KIND LIE IS RIGHT THERE.` → `TWO SIDES, TWO TEXTS.`

segments.voice: The seventh perfection is sacca, truthfulness. Let the strict side speak first. In one discourse the Buddha shows his son Rahula a dipper with a little water left in it, then tosses the water out, then turns the dipper upside down. That empty, he says, is the practice of anyone who isn't ashamed to tell a deliberate lie. Read this way, the precept against false speech has no exception for kindness. Truth told gently, at the right time, yes. A lie, no. Now the other side: the Lotus Sutra, a Mahayana scripture. A father sees his children playing in a burning house, too absorbed to listen. So he calls out that wonderful carts are waiting outside. They run out, safe. Then the Buddha asks whether the father lied. The answer is no: he saved them, and gave them something even better. The Lotus Sutra calls this skillful means, upaya. Hear the strict side's best case: once kind lies are allowed, who decides which lies are kind? And the other side's: a rule that lets children burn has missed its point. Where they meet: truth is there to serve, never to wound for sport.
screen: `SACCA: THE SEVENTH PERFECTION.` · `VIEW ONE: THE EMPTY DIPPER.` · `VIEW TWO: THE BURNING HOUSE.` · `WHO DECIDES WHICH LIE IS KIND?` · then, large: `TRUE.`

segments.voice: Think of one true thing you've been softening into something not quite true. In your notes or on paper, write how you'd say it exactly and kindly. Read it back once, checking for anything that isn't true and anything that isn't kind.
Sacca: truth, truthfulness, the seventh perfection. Words that match what is, said for the listener's good.
Something to keep: true, one small word with the whole argument folded inside it. Sleep well.

howItsDone: Buddhist lay people take the precept to refrain from false speech among the five precepts; teachers in different schools discuss hard cases, some pointing to the Rahula discourse and some to the Lotus Sutra's skillful means.

match.prompt: two views on truth — tap the pairs.
pairs: a parable in the Lotus Sutra

myth: Buddhist texts speak with one voice about kind lies
the dipper and the burning house pull different ways, and Buddhists still argue it.
in the Lotus Sutra, the father promises carts to get his children out
and gives them something even better.
skillful means is permission to lie for your own benefit
in the Lotus Sutra it's for the listener's good: children out of a fire.

fork.setup: you've always heard that a kind lie is fine. state the strict view at its strongest.
options: once kind lies are allowed, anyone can call their lie kind; truth is safer.
lying is always worse than letting someone get hurt.
the Buddha never spoke about lying, so the rule came later.
fork.reveal: the strict view's best case: who decides which lie is kind? the Lotus Sutra answers with the burning house. both views read texts they hold sacred.

chat.says: Ông asked if his driving's still ok. it… kind of isn't. lie to save his pride?
options: Tell him gently, at a good moment. It's about his safety, and yours.
A kind lie is fine here. His feelings matter most right now.
Say it at dinner in front of everyone so he takes it seriously.
chat.meaning: Both views on truth agree it should serve, not wound. Here the truth protects him, so say it kindly, at the right time.

tie.story: Both views agree: truth is there to serve, never to wound.

Rahula.meaning: the Buddha's son, who became a monk

Lotus Sutra.meaning: a Mahayana scripture full of parables

upaya.meaning: skillful means: fitting the teaching to the listener
